locator.text: Display 123.7, p. 123, in the proof of Lemma 10.5

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The second inequality of the paper's chain, E_R(t) ≤ C_T'/R, is stated with an explicit constant: le_div_radius_of_deriv_le gives E(t) ≤ (C·T·exp(K·T))/R, which with K = 2G and C = D is the paper's C_T'/R, and eq_zero_of_weighted_rate_bound applies it to E_R = weightedEnergy (weight R) (u-v). The first, middle expression is not formed: the Lean's Gronwall uses the constant integrating factor exp(-K t) with a time-uniform K, not the paper's time-dependent factor exp(2∫_s^t ‖∇u(a)‖_∞ da), and so never produces (2C_T/R)∫_0^t exp(2∫_s^t ‖∇u(a)‖_∞ da) ds. The nearest Lean form is E(t) ≤ ε·t·exp(K·t) (le_exp_mul_of_deriv_le), which is the paper's middle integral bounded above by its own constant-coefficient majorant once ‖∇u(a)‖_∞ ≤ K/2; the paper's factors of 2 are consistent, since its display eq-p123-6 divided by 1/2 gives E_R' ≤ 2‖∇u‖_∞E_R + 2C_T/R. I searched decls.jsonl case-insensitively for `gronwall` (44 hits, all inspected by file) and for a signature containing `exp (∫`: every Gronwall-type declaration in the repository (ComparisonGronwall, ScalarEnergyBound.forced_gronwall*, PeriodicUniqueness.gronwall_zero, R3LocalizedEnergyLimit.gronwall_error) takes a constant coefficient K, so no declaration states the Duhamel form. Severity low: the conclusion the paper draws from the display — E_R(t) ≤ C_T'/R uniformly in R, hence w = 0 after R → ∞ — is proved (WholeSpaceEnergyLimit.eq_zero_of_radius_bound, line 53).
